items.title: The hidden network: Inside the phishing infrastructure ecosystem powering global cybercrime | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Analyzes the underground infrastructure supporting large-scale phishing operations, detailing domain generation algorithms, bulletproof hosting networks, and CDN abuse tactics. Provides actionable IOCs and architectural insights for network defenders to block malicious traffic at the DNS and proxy layers before credential harvesting occurs.

items.title: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Dissects the EvilTokens framework, which exploits OAuth device code flows to bypass traditional MFA. Explains how attackers automate token exchange and session persistence, offering detection strategies for identity teams to monitor anomalous device code requests and implement conditional access policies.

items.title: The Hidden Relay: Inside a Device Code Phishing Kit That Never Shows the Code
items.excerpt: Reveals a novel device code phishing kit that operates without displaying the verification code to victims, using background relay techniques to capture tokens. Details the attack chain, infrastructure footprint, and evasion methods. Provides actionable detection logic for SIEM and identity protection platforms.

items.title: Inside Wazza: A Newly Observed Device Code Phishing Kit Targeting Microsoft 365 Accounts
items.excerpt: Examines the Wazza phishing kit, a newly identified tool targeting Microsoft 365 via device code authentication. Highlights its evasion techniques, infrastructure patterns, and user interface cloning methods. Recommends endpoint and identity monitoring controls to detect and mitigate unauthorized device code approvals.

items.title: Device Code Phishing is an Evolution in Identity Takeover | Proofpoint US
items.excerpt: Explores the shift from password harvesting to device code phishing as a primary identity takeover vector. Discusses attacker motivations, campaign mechanics, and the limitations of traditional email security. Outlines defense-in-depth strategies focusing on user training, conditional access, and real-time identity analytics.

items.title: Microsoft 365 device code phishing campaign bypasses password stealing | RL Blog
items.excerpt: Documents a widespread campaign that circumvents traditional password theft by targeting the OAuth device code flow. Explains how attackers leverage legitimate authentication endpoints to steal access tokens. Recommends network segmentation, conditional access rules, and user awareness training to mitigate identity compromise.

items.title: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign | CloudSEK
items.excerpt: Chronicles the BigBear 2.0 campaign leveraging Evilginx2 for reverse proxy phishing. Details how the toolkit intercepts multi-factor authentication challenges and session cookies. Provides network-level detection rules and proxy configuration hardening steps to prevent credential relay attacks.

items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Investigates a campaign using generative AI to craft highly personalized device code phishing lures. Analyzes how AI accelerates campaign scaling and improves social engineering success rates. Offers guidance for security teams to implement AI-aware detection models and strengthen identity verification workflows.

items.title: CVE-2026-126259
items.excerpt: A missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.12, FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.13 may allow an unauthenticated attacker with HA FGSP + standalone-config-sync, or autoscale to execute command as super admin via crafted HA packets.

items.title: CVE-2026-126253
items.excerpt: A authentication bypass by primary weakness vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.12, FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.13 may allow an unauthenticated attacker to broadcast LSA via specially crafted request

items.title: CVE-2026-126251
items.excerpt: A incorrect authorization vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 through 8.0.3, FortiAuthenticator 6.6.0 through 6.6.10 may allow an attacker to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.

items.title: CVE-2026-126777
items.excerpt: Traccar 3.15 before 6.17.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in LdapProvider.login() that fails to reject empty passwords, causing LDAP binds to be performed as unauthenticated binds when LDAP authentication is enabled. Unauthenticated attackers who know a valid username can log in via POST /api/session or HTTP Basic authentication with an empty password against directories that permit unauthenticated binds, obtaining sessions for any account including administrators.

items.title: CVE-2026-126157

items.title: CVE-2026-126150

items.title: CVE-2026-126257
items.excerpt: A use of hard-coded password vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 through 8.0.3, FortiAuthenticator 6.6.0 through 6.6.10 may allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass credential validation in certain circumstances outside of the attacker's control and gain unauthorized access.

items.title: CVE-2026-126241
items.excerpt: A improper neutralization of special elements used in an sql command ('sql injection') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 through 8.0.3, FortiAuthenticator 6.6.0 through 6.6.10 may allow an authenticated attacker to execute unauthorized SQL commands on the underlying database.
